summary:
On a long mission, astronauts are cut off from the people they love, and with no one watching, it’s easy to let daily health habits slip. Space Sprout is a cozy space-station game that tackles both at once by giving everyone a garden to share.

The astronaut and their family back on Earth live together on the same little station, which has three rooms: a garden, a medical bay and a social space. Everyone does their own health check-ins (heart rate, sleep, exercise, mood and so on), whether by syncing a wearable or typing the numbers in, and every check-in earns seeds. The whole family pools those seeds to plant and tend the garden together, growing crops like mustard and lettuce, the same ones astronauts actually grow in orbit. So the astronaut is never building healthy habits alone, because the people at home are doing it right alongside them.

Nothing in the game is about judgment. Plants never wilt as punishment, and there are no scores and no diagnoses. Each person’s health data stays private to them; the station only ever finds out about the seeds. Messages and emotes are always free, so keeping in touch never depends on anything else.

The idea is simple: looking after yourself should feel like caring for something you share with the people you love.
details:
What it does. Space Sprout is a game set on a small space station shared by the astronaut and their family. You can play it in a browser or as a mobile app, in English or Spanish, and the station has three rooms to explore.

In the Medical Station, everyone does a daily check-in covering ten health readings. That includes the astronaut in orbit and the family back on Earth. They can sync a wearable or just type the numbers in. Every check-in earns seeds, up to a daily limit, with bonuses for hitting goals and keeping a streak going. Skipping a day never costs anything. Health Insights shows how each reading has moved over the past week, with plain, neutral explanations: no warning thresholds, no diagnoses.

In the Garden, everyone’s seeds go toward growing fourteen different plant species, and the Supply Store has pots and decorations to make the space your own. When a plant is thriving, it glows softly in its close-up view.

The Social Space has a message board and emotes so the astronaut and their family can stay in touch, and messaging is never locked behind rewards. Friendly crew members and pets wander around the station and stop to ask how everyone’s day went.

Benefits. NASA research suggests that caring for plants helps astronauts deal with the isolation and confinement of spaceflight, which NASA’s Human Research Program counts as one of the main risks of long missions. Space Sprout builds on that idea, with one change: the astronaut doesn’t tend the garden alone, but grows it together with their family back on Earth. That gives astronauts a gentle reason to keep up healthy habits, one that comes from caring for something rather than from pressure. And they aren’t building those habits alone, because their family is taking care of themselves too, on Earth, for the same garden. It also gives everyone an easygoing place to spend time “together” despite the distance.

How we built it. The client uses Angular, Phaser 3 and Tailwind, and we used Ionic to turn that same code into a mobile app. The backend runs on NestJS, TypeORM and PostgreSQL hosted on Neon. A shared TypeScript package holds the game rules, so the client and server always follow the same ones. Each member’s health data is stored privately on the server, and only the seed rewards are shared with the rest of the family. Our design team made all the illustrated art.

What makes it creative. Space Sprout doesn’t show health as a medical dashboard. It turns health into something you grow with your family, with everyone pitching in, and you play together instead of competing.

Try it. Play it in the browser at https://garden.raulmen.dev, or install the Android app from https://github.com/raulmendev/space-sprout/raw/main/deploys/space-sprout.apk. It's available in English and Spanish. The source code is at https://github.com/raulmendev/space-sprout.
